market_rationale: Macro mix is stagflationary-leaning: payrolls weak (29k, prior months revised down 60k) but inflation elevated (PCE 3.4%, ISM prices 77.9), Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% and 10y at 5.28%. SPY sits within 1% of its 52-week high while breadth is narrow (RSP -4.5% vs SPY over 21 sessions, only 26% of assets positive over 5 sessions). Leadership is concentrated in semis/tech; defensives, duration, credit and precious metals have been sold. With yields easing slightly after the soft payroll print and only second-tier data (ISM services, trade, wholesale) before exit, a modest mean-reversion in oversold low-beta pockets is plausible, but the regime offers limited high-conviction edge versus SPY.
portfolio_rationale: Edges are thin. The best risk-adjusted reversal candidates are oversold low-beta defensives: Healthcare (deep relative pullback, zero beta, strong quality score) and Gold (sharp drop into a soft payroll print with yields easing and inflation at 3.4%), both marginally above 55% probability. High yield shows a volume dislocation but low beta limits its excess return, so it falls just below eligibility. Extended tech/semis, crypto, and stretched Brazil lack in-window support; Utilities, South Africa and defense look like persistent downtrends rather than overreactions. Overall SPY near highs with narrow breadth leaves a mild preference for the benchmark.
